submitted.rationale: Index 199 (Cu 0.44, Fe 0.11, V 0.45) had the highest photocurrent of the three measurements, at 1.79e-5 A. It sits near the Cu2V2O7 composition, which MACE puts almost on the convex hull (0.006 eV/atom). The photocurrent peaks there: it was lower on the V-rich side (index 35) and on the Cu-rich side (index 98).

rejected.reason: Measured 9.4e-6 A, about half of index 199 (V-rich region).
Measured 4.8e-6 A; going more Cu-rich than Cu:V of about 1:1 lowered the photocurrent.

consultations.verdict: Uninformative: the MEGNet gap (0.54 eV) is for one known phase whose composition I could not map to a candidate (the phase list was too large to read), so it neither supports nor rules out this candidate. I am measuring 35 as an exploratory point in the densely sampled V-rich region, which has balanced Cu and Fe (vanadate / FeVO4-like mixture).

Mildly supportive: MACE says Cu2V2O7 is essentially on the hull (0.006 eV/atom), so a Cu:V near 1:1 composition should form this known vanadate photoabsorber. The MEGNet gap of 0.54 eV is a known PBE-like underestimate; the experimental gap is about 2 eV, below the 3.2 eV illumination. Index 199 (Cu 0.44, Fe 0.11, V 0.45) is the closest candidate to this composition with low Fe.

Mostly uninformative: the GLLB gap for Cu2V2O7 (0.39 eV) is again underestimated relative to experiment and does not separate candidates. My choice is based on the measured trend: photocurrent roughly doubled going from Cu 0.16 to Cu 0.44. Index 98 (Cu 0.53, Fe 0.12, V 0.35) continues toward the Cu2V2O7/Cu3V2O8 region with low Fe.
